content: An article from News roundup Arcus kidney cancer data impresses analysts; TriGemX inks a SPAC deal New follow-up results suggest Arcus’ drug might be superior to a marketed Merck medicine. Elsewhere, Eli Lilly and AstraZeneca forged new partnership deals. Published Oct. 21, 2026 Ben Fidler Lead Editor Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving Arcus Biosciences and Eli Lilly, as well as updates from TriGemX Bio and AstraZeneca that you may have missed. Shares of Arcus Biosciences climbed 8% Tuesday on updated results that bolstered investor and analyst confidence in the company's experimental kidney cancer drug. Arcus' experimental therapy casdatifan is currently in late-stage testing and works similarly to Merck & Co.'s marketed kidney cancer drug Welireg. At an R&D day, the company presented follow-up results from earlier-line tests in multiple settings that, combined, suggested casdatifan provides a “step-up in potency” compared to Welireg, wrote Leerink Partners analyst David Risinger. To Mizuho Securities' Salim Syed, the findings on tumor progression and survival indicated investors should ascribe potential value to casdatifan in the first-line setting. Lipid nanoparticles — microscopic, fatty shells — are commonly used in RNA-based therapies and other forms of genetic medicine. Through the collaboration, METiS will use AI to help Lilly come up with new lipid nanoparticles capable of “tissue-specific delivery,” the companies said. Lilly could pay METiS up to $1.1 billion in the deal, though the companies didn’t say how much of that cash is guaranteed. TriGemX Bio will go public by merging with a blank-check company created by life sciences investment firm TCGX. The “SPAC” deal announced Monday will equip TriGemX with $246 million in cash, consisting of the $86 million in the acquisition vehicle’s reserves and a $160 million investment from a handful of prominent firms. TriGemX initially formed as Kallyope to target the “gut-brain axis,” a communication channel between cells in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract. It’s since rebranded, sold off obesity drug programs and now has a therapy called elismetrep in late-stage testing for acute migraines. AstraZeneca and Oracle Health and Life Sciences are working together in an AI-focused partnership aimed at optimizing clinical trials. Through the partnership, the two companies will test “practical ways” to connect drug research to health care, they said in a Tuesday announcement. Their first test will involve supporting research in Abu Dhabi, where the partners hope to help experts better identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension and improve recruitment in clinical trials. title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. Neither release addresses market reaction, and independent verification of the platform’s performance in these indications was not available at the time of publication.SourcesAstraZeneca announces new strategic collaboration with insitro to use advanced AI systems to develop transformative therapeutics for difficult to treat cardiometabolic diseases. About one in four drugs launched in 2025 had an annual net price exceeding $500,000, while another 34% were priced between $200,000 and $500,000. At the same time, though, the most substantial increase in net launch prices occurred between 2022 and 2023; last year, there was a 2% decline.Advertisement Novo Nordisk disclosed that its next-generation experimental drug, CagriSema, showed 25% weight loss on average in women with obesity or overweight in a late-stage study, according to Reuters. CagriSema, viewed ‌as a successor to its big-selling weight loss drug Wegovy, could help Novo claw back ground lost to Eli Lilly in the weight loss market. Wegovy faces ​patent expirations after 2030. Novo said a 2.4-milligram dose of CagriSema ​was associated with an average weight loss of 25% after ⁠68 weeks in 2,309 women, ​compared with 3% weight loss in women on placebo. content: October 23, 2026 09:00 AM EDTUpdated 03:02 PM DealsChina Did the US just kill off Chi­na biotech deals? Drew Armstrong Executive Editor Thurs­day night, the Trea­sury De­part­ment is­sued a pro­posed rule to im­ple­ment the COINS Act, the 2025 law that gov­erns US in­vest­ment in sen­si­tive tech­nolo­gies in Chi­na and oth­er coun­tries. In a sur­prise turn, a broad set of drug tech­nolo­gies made the list of pro­hib­it­ed in­vest­ments. Chi­na deal­mak­ing has been the back­bone of bio­phar­ma M&A over the past two years, cre­at­ing dozens of new com­pa­nies and part­ner­ships. It’s al­so been the most di­vi­sive is­sue in biotech, with some ar­gu­ing for a free flow of drugs, ideas and deals, and oth­ers in­sist­ing the trans­ac­tions need to be shut down. Play­ing this video loads YouTube, which sets ad­ver­tis­ing cook­ies. Watch on YouTube On Post-Hoc Live, my col­league Max Bay­er and I talked about what the rule says, what it means for biotech, what we know, what we don’t and what hap­pens next. You can watch our con­ver­sa­tion on YouTube. You can al­so lis­ten to the episode on Spo­ti­fy or Ap­ple Pod­casts. We dug in­to whether the rule will re­al­ly kill off Chi­na deals and how the in­dus­try is re­act­ing, and talk about our lat­est re­port­ing on this fast-de­vel­op­ing sto­ry. It was a great con­ver­sa­tion, and I hope you’ll give us a lis­ten. — Drew Arm­strong, Ex­ec­u­tive Ed­i­tor AUTHOR Drew Armstrong Executive Editor drew@endpointsnews.com @ArmstrongDrew Drew Armstrong on LinkedIn

MADRID — A personalized mRNA cancer vaccine reduced the risk of disease recurrence in patients with melanoma by 42% compared to a standard treatment, according to a large clinical trial conducted by the drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The results are an important advance for the treatment of melanoma, oncologists said, because patients lived significantly longer without their cancer returning. Advertisement The success of the Moderna-Merck vaccine, intismeran autogene, may also usher in a new wave of treatments for other types of cancer, though experts are debating how broadly applicable the technology could be. The medicine is an individualized therapy that attacks the unique mutations, called neoantigens, found in a patient’s tumor. The approach is made possible by the same mRNA technology that led to the rapid development of vaccines against Covid-19. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: STAT Plus: AbbVie skin disorder drug succeeds in late-stage trial, but results miss market expectations
content: STAT PlusBiotech AbbVie skin disorder drug succeeds in late-stage trial, but results miss market expectations Findings dim hopes lutikizumab can compete with UCB’s Bimzelx Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Jonathan WosenOct. 22, 2026 West Coast Biotech & Life Sciences Reporter Jonathan Wosen[email protected]Jonathan Wosen is STAT’s West Coast biotech & life sciences reporter. You can reach Jonathan on Signal at jwosen.27. AbbVie reported on Thursday that an experimental therapy for hidradenitis suppurativa, a chronic skin condition, succeeded in a late-stage trial but missed market expectations, leaving experts doubtful the drug can compete with the current standard of care. In the Phase 3 Intrepid trial, which enrolled 1,400 patients with moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa, 31.4% of participants given weekly injections of AbbVie’s therapy, lutikizumab, reported a 75% or greater reduction in the number of inflamed bumps and abscesses across their skin, compared to 23.4% of those in the placebo group after 16 weeks. This measure was the study’s primary endpoint.Advertisement The company also reported that the drug met eight secondary endpoints, including improvements in skin pain and flares. Lutikizumab was generally safe and well tolerated, with adverse event rates that were nearly identical between the placebo and treatment groups. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 21, 2026 FDA Approves Hibsago (Bepirovirsen) for Chronic Hepatitis B Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff The FDA approved GSK's bepirovirsen for adults with chronic hepatitis B on nucleoside therapy, based on phase 3 trials showing 19% functional cure. Advertisement The FDA has approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen), GSK’s antisense oligonucleotide, for adults with chronic hepatitis B who are already taking nucleoside analogue therapy.1 The decision follows approval in Japan and extends the drug to a U.S. patient population GSK estimates at about 1.7 million people.1 Hibsago offers a fixed-duration option aimed at functional cure, which suppressive therapy rarely achieves.1“Despite current therapies, many people living with chronic hepatitis B remain on treatment indefinitely and continue to face the risk of serious liver complications. For the first time, with Hibsago, US patients have the potential to achieve functional cure after a six-month treatment course, with the added convenience of the option of self-administration after the first dose,” said Tony Wood, chief scientific officer at GSK.1Key FactsHibsago (bepirovirsen), antisense oligonucleotideIndication: Chronic hepatitis B in adults (add-on)Action: FDA approval, Oct. 20, 2026Trials: B-Well 1 and 2, phase 3, placebo-controlledEfficacy: 19% functional cure vs 0% on placeboSafety: Injection-site redness, pain, enzyme riseStatus: Approved in U.S. and JapanWhat does the FDA approved indication cover?The indication covers adults without cirrhosis who have received a nucleoside analogue for at least six months, have a suppressed viral load and have surface antigen levels of 3,000 IU/mL or lower, as determined by an FDA-authorized test.1 The agency granted the approval under priority review and Breakthrough Therapy designation.1 Quantitative surface antigen testing determines eligibility, and GSK said several tests are available, including one recently authorized by the agency.1What did the B-Well phase 3 trials show?The approval rests on B-Well 1 and B-Well 2, two replicate, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in adults on nucleoside analogue therapy across 29 countries.1,2 Participants received bepirovirsen 300 mg weekly by subcutaneous injection or placebo for 24 weeks.2In pooled data, 233 of 1,220 treated participants (19%) achieved functional cure, compared with none of 614 on placebo.1 Rates were 20% in B-Well 1 and 19% in B-Well 2 at week 72.2 Among participants with surface antigen at or below 1,000 IU/mL, 200 of 768 (26%) reached functional cure, versus none of 393 on placebo.1 Functional cure means viral DNA and surface antigen remain undetectable for at least 24 weeks after all treatment stops, consistent with guidance from a joint American and European liver disease society conference.1,3 (()=>{var The most frequent adverse events were injection-site redness, local pain and a temporary rise in a liver enzyme.1Why does functional cure matter in chronic hepatitis B?Chronic hepatitis B affects more than 240 million people worldwide and causes roughly 1.1 million deaths a year, GSK said.1 Nucleoside analogues have been standard of care for decades and produce functional cure in about 1% of patients, according to Pharmaceutical Technology, so many patients remain on treatment indefinitely.1,4GSK licensed bepirovirsen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals and developed it in collaboration with that company.1 GlobalData, which owns Pharmaceutical Technology, projects sales of $926 million in 2034 in a chronic hepatitis B market it expects to reach $3.2 billion that year.4 Competition is emerging: Gilead Sciences’ selgantolimod is in late-stage trials.4What are the limitations, and what comes next?About four in five treated participants did not meet the functional cure definition, and the trials compared bepirovirsen with placebo rather than with other investigational agents.1,2 The indication excludes patients with cirrhosis and those with surface antigen above 3,000 IU/mL, a narrower group than the full chronic hepatitis B population. GSK said participants at or below 1,000 IU/mL represent about 45% of diagnosed cases globally.1 The B-Well primary endpoint was functional cure. Bristol Myers Squibb on Friday reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research. title: Biohaven’s previously rejected rare disease drug to get fresh FDA review
content: An article from Biohaven’s previously rejected rare disease drug to get fresh FDA review U.S. regulators have accepted a new submission for Vyglxia, offering the chance at a turnaround for another rare disease medicine spurned by previous FDA leadership. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 艾伯维乌帕替尼获批重度斑秃治疗！国内适应症增至9项，全球年销83亿美元的JAK1抑制剂再扩容 艾伯维乌帕替尼获批重度斑秃治疗！国内适应症增至9项，全球年销83亿美元的JAK1抑制剂再扩容 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/10/19 3986 AbbVie Inc 乌帕替尼 JAK1 凌科药业（杭州）有限公司 江苏先声医药科技有限公司 10月15日，NMPA官网显示，艾伯维的乌帕替尼缓释片获批新适应症，用于治疗成人及12岁及以上青少年重度斑秃患者。摩熵医药数据库显示，这是该药在国内获批的第9项适应症。图源：NMPA官网乌帕替尼是一款选择性JAK1抑制剂，也是艾伯维免疫领域的核心产品。2025年，该药全球销售额达83.04亿美元；2026年上半年销售额达46.44亿美元。艾伯维预计，其2027年销售额有望超过110亿美元。一、适应症扩至9项，三项新适应症申请在审乌帕替尼于2019年首次在美国获批上市，商品名为Rinvoq。2022年2月，该药首次在中国获批，此后逐步拓展适应症。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库截至目前，乌帕替尼在国内已获批9项适应症，涵盖特应性皮炎、类风湿关节炎、银屑病关节炎、溃疡性结肠炎、克罗恩病、强直性脊柱炎、放射学阴性中轴型脊柱关节炎、巨细胞动脉炎及重度斑秃。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库此外，乌帕替尼用于幼年型银屑病关节炎、多关节性幼年特发性关节炎及非节段型白癜风的上市申请，均已进入CDE审评审批阶段。剂型方面，艾伯维还开发了面向儿童患者的乌帕替尼口服溶液，其上市申请已于2026年8月25日获CDE受理。二、III期研究显示，重度斑秃患者毛发覆盖率改善乌帕替尼重度斑秃适应症本次获批，基于III期Up-AA研究（NCT06012240/CTR20233956）的积极结果。该研究由研究1、研究2两项关键性研究组成，均为随机、双盲、安慰剂对照设计。该适应症已于2026年7月在欧盟获批。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2025年7月，艾伯维公布研究2的积极结果。第24周时，乌帕替尼15 mg组和30 mg组分别有44.6%和54.3%的患者达到SALT评分≤20，即头皮毛发覆盖率达到80%及以上；安慰剂组这一比例为3.4%。在头皮毛发覆盖率达到90%及以上（SALT评分≤10）方面，两剂量组的达标率分别为36.0%和47.1%，安慰剂组为1.4%。2025年8月公布的研究1结果同样积极。第24周时，15 mg组和30 mg组达到SALT评分≤20的患者比例分别为45.2%和55.0%，安慰剂组为1.5%；达到SALT评分≤10的患者比例分别为35.2%和45.8%，安慰剂组为0.7%。两项研究均达到主要终点，并达到包括眉毛、睫毛改善及头皮毛发完全覆盖在内的其他关键次要终点。安全性方面，两种剂量的总体安全性特征与乌帕替尼既往已获批适应症中的观察结果一致。三、JAK1赛道竞争升温，国产药加速追赶据摩熵医药数据库显示，目前全球有22款JAK1单靶点抑制剂进入临床开发阶段，其中13款由中国企业开发，国内企业占比超过半数。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库在国内已获批的JAK1抑制剂中，乌帕替尼凭借9项适应症形成较广泛的疾病覆盖。其他产品则各有布局：迪哲医药的戈利昔替尼主要布局淋巴瘤领域；辉瑞的阿布昔替尼目前获批1项适应症；恒瑞医药的艾玛昔替尼于2025年3月获批，目前已覆盖5项适应症。此外，凌科药业与先声药业合作开发的泽普昔替尼已在国内申报上市，另有6个项目处于III期临床阶段。随着乌帕替尼在国内获批第9项适应症，以及国产JAK1抑制剂持续推进临床开发和适应症拓展，国内JAK1抑制剂市场的竞争将进一步加剧。对于相关企业而言，适应症布局、临床证据及差异化定位，将成为后续竞争的重要因素。参考来源：[1] 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/10/23 3091 巴托利单抗 FCGRT IgG 和铂医药（上海）有限责任公司 石药集团有限公司 10月22日，国家药监局官网显示，石药集团/和铂医药申报的进口1类新药巴托利单抗注射液获批上市，用于治疗全身型重症肌无力（gMG）。图源：NMPA官网一、历经两次上市申报，巴托利单抗终于获批巴托利单抗（HBM9161）是一款全人源抗新生儿Fc受体（FcRn）单克隆抗体，可阻断FcRn与免疫球蛋白G（IgG）结合，加速体内IgG清除，从而减少致病性IgG介导的自身免疫反应。在全身型重症肌无力III期临床研究中，巴托利单抗取得积极结果。2021年1月，该药被CDE纳入突破性治疗药物程序。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库巴托利单抗的权益合作始于2017年9月。当时，和铂医药从HanAll Biopharma获得包括巴托利单抗在内的两款创新生物制品在中国（包括香港、澳门和台湾）的开发、生产及商业化权益。2022年10月，和铂医药与石药集团全资子公司恩必普药业有限公司达成合作协议，在中国共同开发巴托利单抗。其中，和铂医药负责该药针对全身型重症肌无力的完整临床试验设计与执行，并根据产品年度净销售额获得分层销售提成。在上市申报方面，巴托利单抗注射液于2023年6月首次获NMPA受理，受理号为JXSS2300049。此后，因III期临床试验延期，相关申请被主动撤回。2024年7月，相关方重新递交上市申请，受理号为JXSS2400060。历经两年多审评，该药终于于2026年10月获批上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库二、FcRn靶点已有多款药物获批，市场竞争持续近年来，FcRn抑制剂逐步成为全身型重症肌无力治疗领域的重要研发方向，国内已有多款相关药物获批。2023年7月，Argenx与再鼎医药合作开发的艾加莫德α获批进口。2025年3月，优时比的罗泽利昔珠单抗获批进口。该药是全球首个同时覆盖乙酰胆碱受体（AChR）抗体阳性和肌肉特异性酪氨酸激酶（MuSK）抗体阳性全身型重症肌无力患者的FcRn抑制剂。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库随着巴托利单抗获批，国内全身型重症肌无力治疗领域再添一款FcRn靶向药物。后续其临床应用及市场表现，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] Remember, a prescription is not required. Our choice today is ginger peach. Meanwhile, here are a few items of interest. Hope you have a smashing day and, of course, do stay in touch. … Over the last year, a few telehealth companies have begun to market off-label prescriptions of GLP-1 drugs, both branded and compounded, to treat alcohol use disorder and other addictions, STAT tells us. Addiction medicine experts see the businesses responding to a significant unmet medical need. As early evidence of the drugs’ promise emerges, and personal stories circulate on social media platforms, some patients have explicitly sought out the drugs to cut down on drinking. Still, telehealth platforms marketing GLP-1s for addiction trouble some experts, who say this could cause fragmented care and potentially inappropriate prescriptions as researchers are still working to understand and vet the unproven treatments.Advertisement The U.S. Department of Treasury is poised to issue a proposed rule as early as tomorrow that would subject outbound U.S. licensing deals with Chinese biotech companies to additional regulatory scrutiny under the COINS Act, Endpoints News reports. The Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which was enacted in December 2015, puts some American investment in Chinese technology under Treasury screening. Overall concerns about China’s ambitions and a pervasive anti-pharma view in many parts of Congress and the administration may make it difficult for the pharmaceutical industry to overcome objections, Capital Alpha Partners analyst Rob Smith wrote investors. title: FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's Disease
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 23, 2026 FDA Approves Subcutaneous Induction for Skyrizi in Crohn's Disease Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff FDA approved an at-home induction option for risankizumab-rzaa in adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease, based on the phase 3 AFFIRM trial. Advertisement The FDA today approved a subcutaneous induction regimen for AbbVie's Skyrizi (risankizumab-rzaa) in adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.1 The decision lets patients start treatment at home with an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack instead of an intravenous infusion, and continue with the same device during maintenance.1AbbVie filed for the new regimen April 27 and had said it anticipated approval later in 2026.2 The decision changes how therapy begins, not who is eligible, because intravenous induction remains an option.1 "People living with Crohn's disease need treatments that can deliver meaningful disease control from the start," said Roopal Thakkar, M.D., executive vice president, research and development, chief scientific officer, AbbVie. "With the approval of subcutaneous induction, we are building on the strong efficacy of Skyrizi while giving patients and physicians greater flexibility in how treatment is initiated. This is one more example of how AbbVie continues to advance treatment to better meet the needs of people living with Crohn's disease."Key FactsDrug: risankizumab-rzaa; interleukin-23 inhibitorIndication: Moderate-to-severe Crohn's, adultsAction: FDA approves subcutaneous inductionTrial: Phase 3 AFFIRM, 274 patients, randomized 2:1Week 12 clinical remission: 56% vs 30%Week 12 endoscopic response: 43% vs 15%Safety: No new risks (company-reported)Status: U.S. approval, Oct. 23, 2026What does the new induction regimen involve?The subcutaneous regimen is 720 mg delivered by the OBI induction pack at weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8.1 Patients can still begin intravenously with 600 mg at weeks 0, 4 and 8. Either way, maintenance dosing starts at week 12 and is given by OBI every eight weeks.1 The device was first introduced in 2022 for Crohn's disease maintenance.1Lead investigator Millie D. Long, M.D., of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, said: "When patients and I discuss treatment, they want to know two things: will it work? And how will it fit into their lives? AFFIRM answered the first question, with superior rates of clinical remission and endoscopic response versus placebo during induction with subcutaneous Skyrizi, particularly in patients new to advanced therapy. This approval answers the second. As a physician who has used the Skyrizi OBI, I've seen firsthand the convenience it can offer patients. Now with this approval, patients can start treatment at home and continue the same way through maintenance."What did the phase 3 AFFIRM trial show?AFFIRM randomly assigned 274 adults 2:1 to subcutaneous risankizumab or placebo, and 65% had previously failed advanced therapy.1 The co-primary endpoints at week 12 were clinical remission, defined as a Crohn's disease activity index score below 150, and endoscopic response.1 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); In the total population, 56% of treated patients reached clinical remission versus 30% with placebo, and 43% had an endoscopic response versus 15% (both p<0.001).1 Endoscopic remission, a secondary endpoint, occurred in 26% versus 11%.1Results were stronger in patients without prior advanced therapy failure: 74% versus 27% for clinical remission and 60% versus 15% for endoscopic response. In patients who had failed advanced therapy, the rates were 45% versus 31% and 33% versus 15%.1 AbbVie reported no new safety risks.1How does this fit with earlier risankizumab data?Skyrizi is an interleukin-23 inhibitor that binds the p19 subunit and is also approved for ulcerative colitis, plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis.1 In Crohn's disease, the earlier phase 3 ADVANCE and MOTIVATE trials tested intravenous induction. Clinical remission at week 12 occurred in 45% of patients receiving 600 mg versus 25% with placebo in ADVANCE, and 42% versus 20% in MOTIVATE.3 The trials enrolled different populations, so those figures cannot be compared directly with AFFIRM.Why does Crohn's disease remain a treatment challenge?Crohn's disease is a chronic, progressive condition that most often affects the area between the small intestine and colon, causing persistent diarrhea and abdominal pain, and it can lead to complications or surgery.1 In AFFIRM, advanced therapy referred to biologics or Janus kinase inhibitors, and the 65% prior-failure rate reflects how many participants had already tried earlier treatment without adequate results.1 What are the limitations and next steps?The advanced therapy-naive subgroup was small, with 65 treated and 33 placebo patients, and the p-values AbbVie reported apply to the total population rather than subgroups.1 The company's description of the results as market-leading is a comparative claim, and the release includes no head-to-head data to support it. Results from AFFIRM's extension periods were not reported in the announcement, and the safety conclusion rests on the sponsor's summary.1FDA also approved revised prescribing information across all indications, advising clinicians to consider tuberculosis evaluation based on clinical judgment; no test is mandatory before treatment.1 Liver monitoring guidance for Crohn's disease remains in the label.1SourcesAbbVie. 注射液）是一款重组全人源抗IL-4Rα单克隆抗体，其能够特异性结合细胞表面人IL-4Rα，同时阻断IL-4和IL-13信号通路，调控2型免疫，降低嗜酸性粒细胞和IgE水平，从而可用于2型免疫介导的哮喘、特应性皮炎、慢性鼻窦炎伴鼻息肉、慢性自发性荨麻疹、过敏性鼻炎等具有IL-4、IL-13高表达的自身免疫相关疾病。（5）齐鲁制药三抗1类新药QLS-2401获批临床10月14日，齐鲁制药自主研发的1类创新生物药QLS2401注射液获得国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心（CDE）临床试验默示许可，拟定适应症为转移性去势抵抗性前列腺癌（mCRPC）。QLS2401是一款同时靶向PSMA、STEAP1及CD3的三特异性T细胞衔接器（TCE），其同时靶向前列腺癌两个关键抗原，旨在解决前列腺癌的异质性，克服抗原丢失导致的耐药问题。此次获得临床试验默示许可，标志着该产品正式进入临床开发阶段。（6）百利天恒HER2 总体概况根据摩熵医药数据库统计，2026.10.12-2026.10.18期间共有113个创新药/改良型新药临床申请/上市申请获国家药品监督管理局药品审评中心（CDE）承办（按受理号统计，不含补充申请）。其中国产药品受理号90个，进口药品受理号23个。本周共计60款创新药/改良型新药临床试验申请获得“默示许可”，包括化学药24款，生物药36款，无中药。其中值得注意的有：（1）注射用AN-40352026年10月12日，CDE官网公示：阿诺生物申报的注射用AN-4035获得临床试验默示许可，用于携带RAS突变且富集CEACAM5表达的晚期或转移性实体瘤（包括但不限于结直肠癌、胰腺导管腺癌和非小细胞肺癌）。公开资料显示，AN-4035是一款CEACAM5靶向抗体偶联药物（ADC），搭载泛RAS(ON)抑制剂，旨在实现肿瘤选择性RAS通路抑制。AN4035通过将高活性的泛RAS(ON)抑制剂与CEACAM5靶向抗体偶联，旨在将泛RAS(ON)抑制剂选择性递送至肿瘤组织，在实现RAS通路有效抑制的同时，尽可能减少对正常组织的影响。（2）YKYY-036注射液2026年10月13日，CDE官网公示：悦康药业申报的YKYY-036注射液获得临床试验默示许可，用于肥胖或超重。公开资料显示，YKYY-036是一款偶联N-乙酰半乳糖胺（GalNAc）配体的化学合成双链siRNA药物，通过RNA干扰机制靶向抑制素亚基βE（INHBE）基因转录产生的信使RNA（mRNA），介导INHBE mRNA降解，抑制INHBE蛋白翻译，进而减少同源二聚体激活素E（Activin E）的生成。（3）SNA-01注射液2026年10月14日，CDE官网公示：中国科学院生物物理研究所与科兴集团联合申报的SNA-01注射液获得临床试验默示许可，用于即将进入或出生在第一个呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）感染季的新生儿和婴儿预防RSV引起的下呼吸道感染，以及即将进入第二个RSV感染季的高危婴幼儿预防由RSV引起的下呼吸道感染。公开资料显示，SNA-01是一款长效抗呼吸道合胞病毒（RSV）单克隆抗体，通过靶向RSV融合蛋白（F蛋白）发挥中和作用，提供被动免疫，并通过Fc段改造延长半衰期。该产品以单次肌肉注射提供覆盖一个RSV流行季的保护为研发目标，以提升用药便利性和可及性。本周1款新药获批上市。2026年10月16日国家药品监督管理局发布监管公告：国家药品监督管理局批准广州悦康生物制药有限公司申报的中药1.1类中药创新药紫花温肺止嗽颗粒上市。获批适应症为：疏风止咳、温肺化痰之功效，主治感染后咳嗽（风寒恋肺证）。1.1.2 content: An article from Emerging biotech In the hunt for reverse merger targets, Caribou could be prized game The struggling cell therapy developer is exploring strategic alternatives, which, among other characteristics, make it a likely candidate to receive reverse merger interest. In a statement, Caribou CEO Rachel Haurwitz said the current financing environment has made it “increasingly challenging” to secure the money needed to advance the company’s two main research programs, which focus on a hard-to-make form of medicine known as “off-the-shelf” cell therapy. As such, Caribou has made the “difficult decision” not to further develop its programs and to “evaluate strategic alternatives” — common corporate lingo for opening itself up to various deals. Caribou’s board of directors has already cleared management to start evaluating a potential merger, acquisition, business combination or other transactions. The company has also tapped Wedbush Securities to serve as its exclusive financial advisor in this process. To Daina Graybosch, an analyst at Leerink Partners who covers Caribou, the natural end for the company now is either a reverse merger or an acquisition by Tang Capital, a San Diego-based investment firm that made a name for itself by buying up cash-rich biotechs and returning much of their value to shareholders. Caribou ended the second quarter with $114 million worth of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. “I think Rachel and the team really do believe in their assets, but it's a real struggle,” Graybosch said. “And when you finally do raise [capital], it just gets more and more dilutive. To pull the trigger now and give money back is what everybody likes to see” and “creates so much positive trust” with investors. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Caribou checks some of the boxes that, according to deal experts, make for a good reverse merger candidate. It trades on the Nasdaq, for example, which is more attractive to private drug developers than lower-tier, over-the-counter markets. A researcher works in Caribou's labs, where the company was designing cell therapies for blood malignancies. Permission granted by Caribou Biosciences Caribou may also have a subzero enterprise value, which, in broad strokes, means that after accounting for its cash pile, the market is attributing nothing — or, really, less than nothing — to the company’s core operating business. That can actually be a plus to private developers, as it signals they might not have to pay a big premium to snag the public vehicle. Using its June 30 financials and closing share price Wednesday, Caribou would have a negative enterprise value of roughly $20 million. (Notably, that’s at the low end of a range from Leerink, which estimates the figure could be as much as $30 million depending on how much cash Caribou spent in the third quarter.) “I would definitely say a reverse merger is on the table here,” said Emmett Sweeney, a vice president on the healthcare investment banking team at Raymond James. Perhaps what makes Caribou such an obvious reverse merger prospect is it publicly stating that it’s exploring strategic alternatives. When companies do that, they become “low-hanging fruit” for reverse merger deals, according to David Kellman, a managing director and head of life sciences and biopharma investment banking at Citizens. They’re “basically running auction processes” with private companies, Kellman said in an interview earlier this month. “Those are the most obvious candidates, regardless of other criteria.” Caribou’s statement, including the mention of Wedbush being its strategic advisor, is a sign that company leaders are “serious” and “mean business,” Sweeney said. Clearly, “they want to move quickly. That's another aspect of Caribou that makes it an attractive merger partner.” Sweeney and others anticipate that Caribou, if not already, will soon be inundated with inbounds from private companies interested in merging. With roughly two dozen biotech reverse mergers announced this year, “the question for many companies is no longer whether the structure works, but whether they can find the right shell and execute the transaction on attractive terms,” Raymond James analysts wrote in a note to clients Wednesday. One lingering question is whether Caribou’s now-discontinued drugs will find a new home. Graybosch doesn’t have high hopes — in part because of rival programs advancing at other cell therapy developers like Fate Therapeutics and AvenCell Therapeutics, both of which are backed by major life sciences investors and large pharmaceutical firms. “Very rarely do these assets show up [again],” she said. “If I'm an investor thinking, ‘Do I wrap a new company around this asset, or do I go invest in AvenCell or Fate,’ I probably choose AvenCell or Fate at this point.” Recommended Reading A booming business on Wall Street would love more biotechs to quietly die By Jacob Bell • Sept. 10, 2026 Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: Deals

副主编HR+/HER2−晚期乳腺癌后线治疗的考量因素与精准选择HR+/HER2−晚期乳腺癌后线治疗的考量因素与精准选择Q1：HR+/HER2−晚期乳腺癌的治疗选择越来越丰富，从内分泌治疗、CDK4/6抑制剂，到口服SERD、PI3K/AKT通路抑制剂及ADC等，临床医生面临的选择也越来越多。您认为，在患者一线治疗失败后，应主要依据哪些因素选择后续治疗？面对不同作用机制的新药，如何合理安排治疗顺序，让患者获得更长的疾病控制时间？秦文星教授：对于激素受体阳性（HR+）、人表皮生长因子受体2阴性（HER2−）的晚期乳腺癌患者，如今治疗手段日益丰富。一线治疗进展后，需要综合评估多个因素以决定后续方案。首先，需回顾患者的既往治疗史，包括一线治疗所使用的具体药物、既往是否接受过辅助内分泌治疗以及患者辅助治疗的时长。其次，需关注一线治疗的进展特征，是在治疗后短期内快速进展，还是经历较长时间的疾病控制后缓慢进展，这些信息均会影响后续治疗策略的制定。后线治疗方案的制定，主要依据患者的基因检测结果。检测中可能发现雌激素受体1（ESR1）突变、磷脂酰肌醇-3-激酶催化亚基α（PIK3CA）突变、蛋白激酶B（AKT）通路异常等，这些分子特征均可能会直接影响诊疗策略。若检测发现PI3K突变，可考虑使用伊那利塞等新型PI3K抑制剂。如果存在ESR1突变，则可选择新型口服选择性雌激素受体降解剂（SERD）。此外，新型的ADC药物也是重要的后线选择。对于激素受体阳性与三阴性乳腺癌患者，未来的治疗选择将更加多元，临床医生需做好合理的治疗策略，从而为患者带来更优的治疗获益。ADC药物的规范使用与不同靶点载荷的序贯策略Q2：随着ADC在乳腺癌治疗中的应用不断向前推进，临床医生应该如何把握ADC的使用时机？如果患者已经接受过一种ADC，后续是否还可以使用另一种ADC？在选择后续治疗时，需要重点考虑哪些因素？秦文星教授：ADC在乳腺癌诊疗中占据日益重要的地位。对于HER2阳性乳腺癌患者，无论是辅助治疗、新辅助治疗还是晚期治疗阶段，ADC药物均占有重要比重，德曲妥珠单抗（T-DXd）、恩美曲妥珠单抗（T-DM1）等药物已广泛进入临床实践。对于三阴性乳腺癌的患者，既往治疗手段以化疗为主。目前，对于程序性死亡配体1（PD-L1）阴性的患者，可首选戈沙妥珠单抗；对于PD-L1阳性的患者，则可在戈沙妥珠单抗的基础上联合免疫治疗。总体而言，ADC药物已全面融入乳腺癌的临床实践。关于一种ADC药物进展后能否更换另一种ADC药物，未来具备可行性。通过更换不同靶点、不同载荷的ADC药物，仍可能获得较好的疗效，这是后续值得探索的方向。新药临床研究的现实挑战与中国原研药物的期待Q3：从您参与新药临床研究的经验来看，当前乳腺癌患者在接受创新治疗时还面临哪些实际困难？如何让临床研究更贴近患者的真实需求，使患者能够更及时地获得新疗法？此外，您对中国原研乳腺癌新药未来的发展有哪些期待？秦文星教授：在临床研究的实际开展过程中，仍面临一些挑战，比如部分临床研究在一期、二期阶段显示出较好的疗效，但进入三期研究后，疗效并未达到预期。此外，临床研究中可能出现既往尚未被认识的药物新毒性，这些新的毒性一方面考验研究者的应对能力，另一方面也会对患者的生活质量产生影响，需要提前做好预判并进行定期随访。对于中国乳腺癌新药临床研究的未来，应该抱有充分期待。目前，包括ADC药物、双特异性抗体药物、双免治疗等多种创新药物均已进入临床研究阶段，希望这些研究能够尽快取得阳性结果，从而惠及更多患者。责任编辑：肿瘤资讯-Sicily
